cf.title: [BUG] DELETE/UPDATE more than one row in partitioned foreign table

input.subject: [(known) BUG] DELETE/UPDATE more than one row in partitioned foreign table

verdict_reasoning: The goal is not in question: the bug silently changes wrong rows on the remote side, and messages #1 and #6 report production hits. The surviving objections are all fixable level 2 points. The decisive one is maintenance-fit-1: v5-0001 passes an attribute number outside min_attr..max_attr through the planner, and no planner committer has reviewed it. prior-attempts-1 leaves the stable-branch fix open, which the list must settle before commit.

brief.title: postgres_fdw: identify remote rows by ctid and remote tableoid
brief.problem: When a foreign table points to a remote partitioned table or inheritance parent, a non-direct UPDATE or DELETE identifies the remote row by ctid alone. Rows in different partitions can share a ctid, so postgres_fdw changes or deletes rows that do not match the query. Users of postgres_fdw on remote partitioned tables get silent logical corruption on the remote side, a bug known since 2018.
brief.proposed_design: The current patch set (v5) has two parts. v5-0001 lets an FDW add a row-identity pseudo-column outside the normal attribute range to the planner; v5-0002 makes postgres_fdw fetch the remote tableoid this way and send "WHERE ctid = $1 AND tableoid = $2". It also fetches columns one by one and builds the whole row locally, in place of shipping ROW().
user_visible_surface: Remote SQL for every non-direct UPDATE/DELETE in postgres_fdw now selects tableoid and adds "AND tableoid = $2", visible in EXPLAIN VERBOSE.
C API: planner support for FDW-injected row-identity pseudo-columns, with attribute number RemoteTableOidAttributeNumber (MaxHeapAttributeNumber + 1).
Former Assert(fdwroutine != NULL) checks in the planner become runtime errors for FDWs.
postgres-fdw.sgml: new notes on no partition pruning for per-row commands and on chained foreign tables not being protected.
EXPLAIN shows (t.*)::t IS NULL in some whole-row filters on foreign partitions.
author_claims: The patch fixes the wrong-row UPDATE/DELETE for a foreign table on a remote partitioned or inherited table.
v5-0001 has no effect unless an FDW uses it.
The tableoid condition is cheap: about 10% more per remote statement (reviewer measurement).
On a plain remote table there is no measurable slowdown; with 100 partitions per-row commands cost about ten times more, because they go through the root.
Chained foreign tables (ft -> ft -> partitioned) are not detected and stay wrong, as documented.
brief.thread_state: Manuel Reyes Bravo tested v5 and set the entry to Ready for Committer; Jakub Wartak also reviewed. Back-patching is still open: Etsuro Fujita and Michael Paquier favoured a back-patchable remotely_inherited option, and Jakub calls the v5 planner changes invasive.
unclear: No committer who knows the planner has reviewed the v5-0001 changes, as Jakub notes.
The thread does not say what fix, if any, goes to stable branches; varnullingrels use limits v5 to Postgres 16 and later.
The thread does not say whether Etsuro's remotely_inherited option is dropped or still planned alongside v5.
The proposal does not say whether other FDWs are expected to use the new pseudo-column API, or how it is documented for them.

objections.title: Out-of-range pseudo attribute number adds a silent planner invariant
objections.failure_scenario: A later planner patch indexes per-attribute arrays such as attr_needed or attr_widths by attno, assuming the range min_attr..max_attr. It does not handle RemoteTableOidAttributeNumber. On a production build, postgres_fdw UPDATE/DELETE on a remote partitioned table then reads out of bounds or plans wrongly, and nobody notices until a user reports it.
objections.argument: v5-0001 touches costsize.c, initsplan.c, setrefs.c, relnode.c and ruleutils.c so that one attribute number outside the normal range can pass through. Message #36 turns some existing Asserts into runtime errors, but only at places that already had a check. Message #27 asks for a planner expert and message #34 says the reviewer can no longer follow the edge cases. No planner committer has reviewed v5-0001 in the thread, although message #29 says Robert Haas suggested the approach off-list.
objections.author_must_show: Which planner code paths assume attno lies within min_attr..max_attr, and what makes a future patch that misses the pseudo-column fail in tests instead of in the field?

critic.reasoning: The planner sizes per-attribute arrays by min_attr..max_attr, so an attribute number above that range needs special handling wherever they are indexed. Messages #27 and #34 say no planner expert has reviewed this, and the proposal does not show a loud failure if a later patch misses it.

objections.title: Same non-back-patchable shape that reportedly stalled the earlier fix
objections.failure_scenario: A user on Postgres 16 to 19 runs a non-direct UPDATE on a foreign table over a remote partitioned table. Rows with a shared ctid in other partitions are silently changed. The user finds out later from wrong data, because v5 changes the planner and only lands in 20.
objections.argument: Message #1 reports that the 2018 fixes lost attention partly because they needed new FDW features and could not be backported. Message #9 says this line of work builds on that earlier design and is not back-patchable. v5 keeps that shape: planner changes that message #34 calls invasive, and varnullingrels use that limits it to 16 and later (message #27). Etsuro's remotely_inherited patch (messages #9, #10, #14) is the stable-branch answer, but the thread does not say whether it is still planned alongside v5.
objections.author_must_show: What fix goes to stable branches, and is the remotely_inherited patch still planned to be committed alongside v5?

critic.reasoning: Messages #9, #27 and #34 say this line of work is not back-patchable, and the thread does not settle what stable branches get. v5 does not cause the stable-branch bug, so this is a question to settle before commit and stays fixable.

objections.title: Chained foreign tables keep silent wrong-row updates behind a protective-looking plan
objections.failure_scenario: An administrator points a foreign table at a remote foreign table that sits on a partitioned table. EXPLAIN VERBOSE shows "WHERE ctid = $1 AND tableoid = $2", so the administrator trusts the result. Non-direct UPDATE then changes rows in other partitions, and nothing reports it until someone audits the data.
objections.argument: Message #28 shows this case still corrupts data under v5, and that the new condition makes the plan look protected. Message #29 declines a remote relkind check because of an extra round trip per query and documents the gap instead. A documentation note does not reach users who never read it, and the rest of the patch changes this behaviour from silently wrong to correct. The relkind could be checked only on the non-direct UPDATE/DELETE path, once per foreign table and connection, at much lower cost than the patch assumes.
objections.author_must_show: Why could postgres_fdw not check the remote relkind once per foreign table and connection, only for non-direct UPDATE/DELETE, and refuse when it is a foreign table?

critic.reasoning: Message #28 shows the chained case still changes wrong rows while EXPLAIN shows the tableoid condition. Message #29 rejects a relkind check for its cost on every query, which does not answer a check limited to the non-direct path.

objections.title: New FDW planner API is shaped for postgres_fdw and undocumented
objections.failure_scenario: An author of another FDW, for example one for a remote sharded store, sees RemoteTableOidAttributeNumber and uses it for a different row identity. fdwhandler.sgml says nothing about its rules, so the FDW gets whole-row or setrefs errors like those in message #34. Core then has to keep the undocumented behaviour stable in every later release.
objections.argument: The material shows one fixed attribute number named for the remote tableoid, plus the rule that the scan must go through fdw_scan_tlist (message #21). The proposal does not say whether a second pseudo-column, or an FDW other than postgres_fdw, is supported. It also does not add any documentation for FDW authors. Once released, this becomes extension-facing behaviour that the project must keep working.
objections.author_must_show: Is v5-0001 meant as a general FDW API, and if so, where are its rules documented and how does an FDW add more than one row-identity column?

critic.reasoning: The material shows one fixed attribute number named for the remote tableoid and no documentation for FDW authors. The C API may change between major versions, so the stability claim is overstated, but the open question about scope and documentation stands.

refuted.title: Back-branch fix and the remotely_inherited option are not settled with v5
refuted.failure_scenario: Stable branches get remotely_inherited, and users set it on their foreign tables. If HEAD has v5 but no such option, restoring a dump of those tables, or running pg_upgrade, fails at CREATE FOREIGN TABLE with an invalid postgres_fdw option error. Users find out during the major upgrade.
refuted.argument: In messages #9, #13 and #14, Etsuro and Michael favour a back-patchable remotely_inherited option, plus an IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA switch. Message #34 calls v5 invasive, and v5 cannot go below Postgres 16 because it relies on varnullingrels. The proposal does not say whether HEAD keeps, accepts or ignores remotely_inherited. That decision fixes the cross-version contract for postgres_fdw table options, so it has to be made before either patch is committed.
refuted.author_must_show: If stable branches get remotely_inherited, will HEAD with v5 still accept that option so dumps from older releases restore?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs remotely_inherited in stable branches but not in HEAD. Message #13 discusses the option for "HEAD and the stable branches", and the project commits a fix to master before back-patching it, so the restore failure has no path.

refuted.title: Two different fixes may live on across branches
refuted.failure_scenario: Stable branches get the remotely_inherited option from messages #9 and #13, and HEAD gets the tableoid path. Back-patched fixes to postgres_fdw DML then need two versions for years. Users upgrading also find an option that has no effect or has a different meaning in the new major version.
refuted.argument: Messages #9 and #13 favour a back-patchable option. Message #34 says the v5 planner changes are too invasive to back-patch, and message #27 notes that v5 needs Postgres 16 or later. The proposal does not say whether remotely_inherited is dropped, kept only in stable branches, or also added to HEAD to skip the tableoid condition, as message #9 suggests.
refuted.author_must_show: What exactly goes to each stable branch, and does remotely_inherited exist in HEAD alongside the tableoid path or not?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. Its added point, that back-patched fixes need different versions per branch, holds for any change that is not back-patched.

touch_points.reason: v5-0001 adds planner support for FDW row-identity pseudo-columns and the attribute number RemoteTableOidAttributeNumber.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: v5-0001 changes costsize.c, initsplan.c, setrefs.c and relnode.c, and turns planner Asserts into runtime errors.

touch_points.label: backpatchability

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")

questions: Which planner code paths index per-attribute arrays by attno within min_attr..max_attr, and what makes a later patch that misses the pseudo-column fail in tests?
What fix goes to stable branches, and is the remotely_inherited option still planned alongside v5?
Why can postgres_fdw not check the remote relkind once per foreign table and connection, only for non-direct UPDATE/DELETE, and refuse a remote foreign table?
Is v5-0001 meant as a general FDW API, and if so, where are its rules documented and can an FDW add more than one row-identity column?
Has a committer who knows the planner agreed to review v5-0001, given that message #29 says the approach was suggested off-list?

committability.owner_note: v5-0001 needs a committer who knows the planner's per-attribute bookkeeping and setrefs; none has reviewed it in the thread. Etsuro Fujita takes part and knows postgres_fdw, but favoured the remotely_inherited option.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new planner invariant, an attribute number above the normal range, for as long as the FDW pseudo-column support exists. The owner also signs for the choice of what stable branches get.
committability.author_follow_up: The authors posted revisions up to v5, answered review in messages #29 and #36, and kept the entry rebased across three CommitFests.

priority.reason: The bug silently corrupts remote data and has two independent production reports, so it is worth attention now. The entry is Ready for Committer by a tester, but v5-0001 changes several planner files and no planner committer has reviewed it.

provisional_note: Without the code, I could not check how v5-0001 handles every planner array indexed by attno, or whether it extends the existing row-identity path or duplicates it. I also could not check the ABI effect on planner structs.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends postgres_fdw direct modification so that an UPDATE or DELETE that joins foreign tables on the same server is sent to the remote server as one statement, such as `DELETE ... USING`. It also deparses RETURNING lists that refer to columns of the joined relations.

He also asked for more comments, use of the new RelOptKind macros, and a regression test for the non-pushed path. The patch went to Waiting for author because it had bitrotted, no new version came, and the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Asynchronous execution on postgres-fdw
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds a core pre-execution callback mechanism, so that nodes can register callbacks that run just before the ExecProc phase, and uses it to start postgres_fdw remote queries asynchronously, with one running query per foreign server. It also offers three experimental ways to set the fetch size: duration-based adaptation, a byte-limited FETCH, and a fetch_size foreign table option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas marked the entry rejected because a more general solution based on parallel workers was in progress and would largely make this patch obsolete, with the option to revisit it later in the release cycle. Earlier he had objected that the pre-execution callback has the same problems as starting execution in ExecInit, and that queries should start in the first IterateForeignScan() call. Robert Haas and Stephen Frost replied that the design questions were still open, and Stephen Frost did not like that the mechanism was specific to FDWs.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I've marked this as rejected in the commitfest, because others are
working on a more general solution with parallel workers.

precedents_retrieved.title: Async execution of postgres_fdw.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made postgres_fdw send the remote query asynchronously from ExecInitForeignScan, so several foreign scans could run on remote servers at the same time. It wrapped PGconn in a new PgFdwConn struct so that several scans could share one connection, and it cancelled a pending async query when another scan or modification used that connection.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Starting the remote query in ExecInitNode is against the documented FDW API, which says execution must not start before IterateForeignScan is called. Tom Lane added that ExecInitNode only builds runtime structures: a scan may never be iterated, for example on the inner side of a nestloop with an empty outer relation, and parameter values for a parameterized scan are not yet available. He also asked to drop the connection wrapper layer, which caused most of the code churn and added unchecked malloc failures.
matched_queries: postgres_fdw update delete partitioned foreign table
postgres_fdw WHERE CURRENT OF cursor update
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I certainly appreciate that you've put quite a bit of effort into this
but I'm afraid we can't accept it while it's starting to run a query on
the remote side during the ExecInitNode phase.  The query can not start
executing on the remote side until InterateForeignScan is called.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
Reverted commit(s): Fix corner case for a BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger returning OLD.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Previously, ExecInitModifyTable relied on ExecInitJunkFilter,
and thence ExecCleanTypeFromTL, to build the target descriptor from
the query tlist.  While we just checked (in ExecCheckPlanOutput)
that the tlist produces compatible output, this is not a great
substitute for the relation's actual tuple descriptor that's
available from the relcache.  For one thing, dropped columns will
not be correctly marked attisdropped; it's a bit surprising that
we've gotten away with that this long.  But the real reason for
being concerned with this is that using the table's descriptor means
that the slot will have correct attrmissing data, allowing us to
revert the klugy fix of commit ba9f18abd.  (This commit undoes
that one's changes in trigger.c, but keeps the new test case.)
Thus we can solve the bogus-trigger-tuple problem with fewer cycles
rather than more.

No back-patch, since this doesn't fix any additional bug, and it
seems somewhat more likely to have unforeseen side effects than
ba9f18abd's narrow fix.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the list. Inside the thread, message #1 points to the 2018 discussion: its fix was returned with feedback, and the tableoid junk-column approach was reportedly rejected. Message #9 reports a comment that the tableoid condition was added even for non-inherited tables. Message #30 measures no slowdown on plain tables, which answers that point. The chained foreign table limitation (message #15) is documented, and message #17 accepts leaving it out.
Nothing else from the standards and compatibility angle. The patch adds no SQL syntax and no GUC. The remote SQL change uses tableoid, which every supported remote server has.

The proposal changes no persistent or replicated state: no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, pg_upgrade step or wire protocol message. The remote SQL gains a tableoid column and condition, which any remote Postgres server already supports. The ABI effect of v5-0001 on planner structs cannot be checked without the code, and back-patching is already debated in the thread.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect worth objecting to. It adds a tableoid fetch and an "AND tableoid = $2" condition to remote per-row UPDATE/DELETE under the existing user mapping and remote privileges. The fix narrows the rows affected, so it closes a path where a user with UPDATE or DELETE on one remote partition could change rows elsewhere, and it creates no new role, setting or way for a non-superuser to see data. The extra per-row cost through the root is already open to any user allowed to run the statement. Turning planner Asserts into runtime errors makes a misbehaving FDW fail more safely. Without the code, I could not check whether the remote tableoid pseudo-column can show up in user-visible output beyond EXPLAIN VERBOSE.
Hot-path cost on plain remote tables was measured in message #30 with no visible difference, so no performance objection is raised.

Postgres has no existing feature, option or extension that makes non-direct UPDATE/DELETE through postgres_fdw hit the right row on a remote partitioned table, so a committer cannot point to one. The workarounds in the thread (direct modify, one foreign table per remote partition in message #4, the remotely_inherited error option in messages #2 and #9) avoid or refuse the case and do not fix it. Without the code I could not check whether v5-0001 duplicates the existing add_row_identity_var path or extends it.

The material shows real demand for a silent data-corruption bug. Independent users report production hits: Dalibo in message #1 and Postgres Professional in message #6. The bug has been known since 2018, and several committers and reviewers treat it as needing a fix. Concerns about cost and backpatching belong to other angles, not demand.
